newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end higher on short-squeeze after cash buying.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end higher on short-squeeze after cash buying.

text.p: The key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract surged in late trade to close near its session high on Friday after light cash bond buying from investors forced a short-squeeze in the market.
A report in the afternoon that four group firms of a debt-ridden real estate company had gone bankrupt was also supportive, traders said.
"Investors who were sidelined when the market plunged yesterday started to buy today. And this resulted in dealers' short-squeezing," said a dealer at a "Big-Four" brokerage.
The key March contract ended up 0.37 at 125.97.
The March moved in a range of 125.45 and 125.98. A total of 49,996 contracts changed hands.

The report, which was later confirmed, said group firms of Sueno Kosan, a major borrower from failed mortgage firms, have been declared bankrupt. This prompted fears that similar cases may emerge, which would support JGBs, traders said.

But they said the March's topside was capped at 126.00 as its further rise may result in a fall in the coupon rate of new 10-year JGBs from a record low of 2.6 percent for the previously auctioned 193rd issue. The Ministry of Finance is expected to hold a 10-year JGB auction next Tuesday.
"The market prefers the new 10-year JGBs carry a 2.6 percent coupon rate and a price of under par. So buying stopped when the key contract neared 126.00," the dealer said.

In the cash bond market, scattered buying from institutional investors was detected almost across the yield curve, traders said. JGBs with remaining maturities of seven to eight years were well bid, but the 190th-193rd issues, which had been overbought, were weaker, they said.
"We found investors' attitude to be the same as before. They buy after the market falls, but not too far," said a long-term credit bank dealer.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB stood at 2.420 at 0732 GMT. On Thursday, it jumped by 0.075 to 2.445 percent.
Given the Tokyo stock market's recovery above the 19,000 level and weaker sentiment in JGBs, a few operators have started to prepare for a possible rise in Japanese interest rates, traders said.

A major Japanese bank paid seven to 10-year fixed rates while receiving floating rates in interest rate swaps this morning, a European bank dealer said. "That means they see a new scenario for long-term bond yields as the Nikkei is likely to stay above 19,000," he said.
"The market's consensus is a rise in interest rates may only come after the summer, if then," the first dealer said.

The main factor affecting the central bank's monetary policy would be fear of inflation. But that is unlikely to emerge unless the dollar rises to 130 yen or the impact from fiscal tightening from April is less than expected, he said.

Comments by a Finance Ministry official this morning that MOF expects no more large financial failures on the scale of that of Kizu Shinyo Kumiai, a regional credit union that failed in 1995, did not have much effect on the market, traders said.
